channel.description: Recent content in Browser_extension on Best of AI

item.title: Brisk Teaching
item.description:
Teachers can generate lesson materials, adjust reading levels, and draft feedback on student writing. A student-facing feature lets pupils chat with an AI tutor under teacher guidance. It also supports quizzes.

A free plan covers basic features, and paid plans add more. Teachers should check output before using it with students.

MagicSchool and Diffit are alternatives. Brisk Teaching suits educators who work in Google Workspace.

item.title: Deque axe
item.description:
The free axe DevTools browser extension runs on a page and lists issues with the offending element and a suggested fix. The same engine, axe-core, plugs into test frameworks like Cypress, Playwright, and Jest, so teams can catch regressions in continuous integration. Deque’s paid products add guided manual testing and reporting.

Automated checks find only part of all accessibility problems, since things like reading order and meaningful link text need a person. Auditors usually run axe first and then test with a screen reader and keyboard.

item.title: Bardeen
item.description:
Bardeen automates repetitive work that happens on web pages. A user installs the extension, then runs playbooks that click through sites, extract data, and send it elsewhere. Typical uses include scraping lists of people from LinkedIn into Google Sheets, saving a company’s details to a CRM, or sending a meeting summary to Slack.

A natural language builder lets users describe what they want, and the AI assembles the steps, which can be edited. Triggers run automations on a schedule or when something happens, and integrations cover hundreds of apps. Sales and recruiting teams, who spend time moving data between tabs, are heavy users.

item.title: Sider Omni Sidebar
item.description:
Sider began as a browser sidebar for chatting with AI about web pages. Omni Sidebar extends the idea to the whole Mac: a panel that sees the content in the active app and lets users ask questions, summarize, draft replies, or take actions without copying and pasting.

The assistant supports several underlying models and can work with files and screenshots. For people who live in email, documents, and spreadsheets, an assistant that sees the same screen saves steps.

item.title: AIPRM
item.description:
AIPRM saves people from writing prompts from scratch. Its browser extension adds a prompt library to the ChatGPT interface, organized by topic such as SEO, sales, customer support, productivity, and writing. You pick a prompt template, fill in details like your topic or audience, and it sends a detailed, well-structured instruction to the AI. Users can also create, save, and share their own prompts.

The library grew from community contributions, which means quality varies, though ratings and usage counts help identify useful ones. Paid plans add private prompts, team sharing, and prompt management for organizations, plus integrations with other AI tools. It is popular with marketers and SEO professionals who run the same kinds of tasks repeatedly, such as keyword clustering or content briefs.

item.title: Huntr
item.description:
Huntr helps people stay organized during a job hunt. Users save job postings with a browser extension, move them across stages as they apply and interview, and attach notes, contacts, and documents to each one. Reminders prompt follow-ups so opportunities do not slip.

AI features assist with the writing. They can tailor a resume and cover letter to a posting, suggest keywords, and help prepare for interviews. A resume builder and job board aggregator add to the toolset, and career coaches use Huntr to track clients.

item.title: Kaspr
item.description:
Kaspr is a contact data tool for outbound sales. While browsing a LinkedIn profile, a user clicks the Kaspr extension to reveal a professional email address and phone number, then saves the contact to a CRM or a list. It also supports bulk searches and enrichment of existing records.

The company emphasizes European data and compliance with privacy rules like GDPR, and offers ways for individuals to opt out of the database. Credits limit how many contact details a user can reveal each month, and integrations connect with CRMs and sales engagement tools.

item.title: Lusha
item.description:
Lusha helps sales and recruiting teams get in touch with prospects. While viewing a profile on LinkedIn or a company website, a user clicks the Lusha extension to reveal contact information, then saves it to a CRM. A database search finds contacts by role, company size, and industry.

Additional features include intent signals, technology data, and enrichment of existing lists, as well as integrations with Salesforce, HubSpot, and sales engagement tools. The company emphasizes compliance with privacy laws and offers ways for people to opt out.

item.title: Seamless AI
item.description:
Seamless.AI helps salespeople find who to contact. Users search by title, industry, and location, or use a browser extension to look up contacts on websites, and the platform returns emails and phone numbers pulled from public sources and its database. Lists export to CRMs and engagement tools.

Real-time search and enrichment aim to keep data fresh, and intent signals show which accounts may be in a buying cycle. AI features help write outreach and prioritize accounts.

item.title: NaturalReader
item.description:
NaturalReader turns reading into listening. You paste text, upload a document or PDF, or use the Chrome extension to read a web page, and it reads aloud in a voice you choose, with adjustable speed. Highlighting of each word as it is spoken helps learners follow along, and the tool supports many languages and accents. OCR features can read text from images and scanned pages.

It serves education and accessibility needs. Students with dyslexia, ADHD, or visual impairments use it to access materials, professionals use it to review documents on the go, and teachers use it with classroom content. Premium plans offer higher-quality AI voices, more file formats, and commercial use for creating audio, while a free version covers personal use with basic voices.

item.title: Compose AI
item.description:
Compose AI works wherever you type in Chrome. As you write an email or a message, it suggests the next words or sentence, which you accept with a keystroke, similar to code completion in a programming editor. It can also draft whole replies, rewrite text in a different tone, and fix grammar, with a menu of shortcuts for common tasks.

The product came from a startup that focused on autocomplete for writing, and later added generative features that call large language models for longer tasks. It is intended to save keystrokes on repetitive writing such as emails, support replies, and social posts, and to reduce the effort of starting a draft. A free tier covers basic use, with paid plans for more generations and features.

item.title: GrowthBar
item.description:
GrowthBar tries to simplify SEO for people who are not specialists. You enter a keyword, and the tool shows search volume and difficulty, related keywords, and what the top-ranking pages cover, including their headings and word counts. A Chrome extension displays similar data directly in search results, which helps when researching competitors.

The AI content features turn that research into drafts. GrowthBar can generate outlines, blog posts, and meta descriptions, and tools for rewriting and expanding text help refine them. It also includes rank tracking and backlink data, and an AI assistant to help brainstorm topics. The target users are small business owners, freelancers, and agencies that publish content regularly.

item.title: LanguageTool
item.description:
LanguageTool checks writing for spelling, grammar, punctuation, and style, and is notable for its broad language support, including English, German, French, Spanish, Dutch, Portuguese, and many more. It runs as browser extensions, add-ins for Microsoft Word and Google Docs, a desktop app, and an API, so it can check text wherever you write. Many people use it for writing in a second language or switching between languages.

The core engine is open source and can be self-hosted, which appeals to organizations with privacy requirements and to developers who want to integrate a checker. The premium tier adds more advanced style suggestions, tone and clarity feedback, and AI-powered rephrasing, along with higher character limits. Teams can set custom dictionaries and style rules.

item.title: Microsoft Translator
item.description:
Microsoft Translator covers the common translation needs. You can type or paste text, speak into a phone for conversation translation, translate images and documents, and use offline language packs when traveling. Multi-device conversation mode lets several people speak in different languages and see translations on their own screens, which suits meetings and travel.

It’s integrated throughout Microsoft products. Teams offers live captions and translated meetings, Office apps can translate documents and text, and Edge translates web pages. For developers and businesses, Azure AI Translator provides APIs for text, document, and speech translation, with custom models and glossaries, and options to run in containers.

item.title: Moz Pro
item.description:
Moz was one of the earliest SEO software companies, and Moz Pro remains a staple for agencies and in-house marketers. Users research keywords, audit sites for technical problems, track rankings over time, and analyze links, with Domain Authority, Moz’s well-known score, used as a quick measure of a site’s strength.

The MozBar browser extension overlays metrics on search results and web pages, making competitor checks quick. Reporting tools produce client-ready summaries, and newer AI features suggest priorities and help with content. A separate local product manages business listings.

item.title: Sheet+
item.description:
Sheet+ is for spreadsheet users who know what they want but not the syntax. You describe the calculation, such as the total of sales for a region in a given month, and Sheet+ produces the formula with an explanation. You can paste a formula you don’t understand and get a plain-language breakdown, or paste an error and receive suggestions for fixing it.

It extends to related tasks. It can write Google Apps Script automation from a description, generate regular expressions, and create SQL queries, and integrates with Sheets through an add-on so you can work without leaving the spreadsheet. It’s popular with small business owners, analysts, and anyone who finds formulas intimidating.

item.title: Tactiq
item.description:
Tactiq takes a lightweight approach to meeting notes. Instead of sending a recording bot into the call, it runs as a browser extension that captures the meeting’s captions and audio on your device. A live transcript appears in a sidebar as people speak, and you can highlight key moments as the meeting happens. That makes it less intrusive in calls where an unfamiliar bot would raise eyebrows.

After the meeting, AI features produce summaries, action items, and custom outputs from prompts, such as a follow-up email or a status update. The transcript is saved in your account and can be exported to tools like Notion, Google Docs, Slack, and HubSpot. Templates adapt the output for different meeting types, and a search function finds past conversations.

item.title: Guru
item.description:
Guru stores verified knowledge in cards that teams can find where they work. A browser extension and Slack integration surface relevant answers without leaving the page, and experts verify cards on a schedule so that the information stays trustworthy. The idea is a single source of truth for sales, support, and internal teams.

AI search connects to the company’s other sources, such as documents, chat, and ticketing systems, and answers questions in natural language with citations. Analytics show what people search for and which content is stale. Admins control who can see what, and the AI respects those permissions.

item.title: HyperWrite
item.description:
HyperWrite started as a writing tool that predicted and completed text as you typed. It grew into a suite that includes a document editor, a browser extension that works across websites, and tools for rewriting, summarizing, and researching. Users can generate text from prompts and refine it in place.

The company has focused on agents. An assistant can navigate web pages, fill in forms, and complete multi-step tasks in the browser on a user’s behalf, which fits its idea of a personal AI assistant. It supports multiple underlying models.

item.title: MultiOn
item.description:
MultiOn was one of the early companies to build browser-using agents. A user gives an instruction in plain language, and the agent navigates sites, clicks, types, and completes the steps, keeping a session going across pages. Developers could call it through an API to build agents of their own.

The company has talked about moving into a new phase, and directories describe a change of name and focus, though accounts differ. That makes it worth checking the official site to see what is currently available before depending on it.
